2_Introduction: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.7181%, with VOC of 1.1274 V, FF of 77.803%, and JSC of 25.9 mA/cm². The perovskite composition of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. The film was deposited under controlled conditions, involving an initial spin of 1000 rpm (10 s) followed by a second spin at 5000 rpm (40 s). 160 µL CB as the antisolvent was dripped on the film at 10 s before the end of the last procedure. After the whole spin-coating process, the substrate was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice strain relaxation, and cesium (Cs⁺) for improved thermal tolerance and defect suppression at grain boundaries, while the near-ideal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and reduced octahedral tilting minimize non-radiative recombination pathways; its crystallization kinetics are precisely governed by the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, which optimizes nucleation density without inducing premature aggregation, the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent extraction), and the precisely timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s before spin termination), which arrests intermediate solvate phases—particularly the δ-FAPbI₃–DMSO adduct—enabling preferential growth of the photoactive α-phase with enlarged grains and reduced interfacial trap density; subsequent annealing at 110 °C for 25 min completes ligand expulsion, promotes Ostwald ripening, and relieves residual tensile strain, as corroborated by XRD showing complete suppression of PbI₂ residuals (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—indicative of high crystallinity and low microstrain—while PL mapping reveals uniformly high intensity and spatially homogeneous decay lifetimes (>350 ns), confirming uniform carrier generation and suppressed spatially localized non-radiative recombination across the film, and optical microscopy–derived grayscale analysis demonstrates >99.2% surface coverage with sub-50 nm pinhole density, establishing continuous, morphologically robust charge transport pathways that minimize shunt losses and interfacial recombination; collectively, these structural, optical, and morphological advantages—rooted in thermodynamically guided crystallization control and intrinsic compositional stabilization—translate directly into superior photovoltaic performance, yielding VOC of 1.1274 V, JSC of 25.9 mA/cm², FF of 77.803%, and a champion PCE of 22.7181%.
